key_insight: A D-gun Al2O3-TiO2 coating substantially improves the wear resistance of Ti-6Al-4V, and random forest best predicts wear from sliding conditions.
engineering_relevance: This suggests detonation-sprayed ceramic coatings can extend titanium alloy life in aerospace, biomedical, and marine tribological components.
method: Applied ~200 µm Al2O3-TiO2 coating to Ti-6Al-4V using D-gun under controlled gas flow and stand-off conditions.
Measured wear on a pin-on-disc setup per ASTM G99 across 40–100 N load, 100–200 rpm, and 20–40 min against EN31 steel.
Built ANN, KNN, and random forest models to predict wear from process/test parameters.
evidence_signal: SEM showed reduced wear and tribo-layer formation on coated surfaces, and random forest achieved the lowest mean percentage error and mean squared error among the tested models.
watch_item: The reported predictive performance is based on the tested experimental range, so extrapolation to other loads, speeds, or service environments may be unreliable.
paper_title: Tribological enhancement of Al 2 O 3 -TiO 2 D-gun coated Ti-6Al-4V alloy: A machine learning approach
